bills.title: Conversational AI Protections for Minors
bills.summary: Would require operators of 'conversational AI services' to provide nonhuman disclosures to minors (every three hours) and prohibit minors from accessing sexually explicit content, similar to CA's SB 243. Would also restrict engagement optimization for minors (preventing rewards at unpredictable intervals), require development of suicide and self-harm protocols, prohibit representation as a mental health professional, and require privacy and account-management tools for minor users including parental controls and oversight features. No private right of action.

bills.title: AI Communications Privilege
bills.summary: Would provide that a person's communication with an artificial intelligence system is legally privileged if the communication would have been privileged had the advice been sought from a human professional.

bills.title: GenAI Provenance Data Requirements
bills.summary: Would require GenAI providers to embed provenance data in AI-generated content.

bills.title: AI Health Disclosures and Employee Replacement Prohibition
bills.summary: Would require health disclosures for AI use and prohibit replacing employees with AI.

bills.title: AI Advertisement Disclosures for Health Products
bills.summary: Would require disclosures for AI-generated advertisements regarding consumer health products.

bills.title: Digital Replica Rights and GenAI Content Removal
bills.summary: Would provide individual rights to revoke access to their digital replicas and remove unauthorized GenAI-generated content.

bills.title: AI Model Data Access and Interoperability
bills.summary: Would require AI model operators to provide users with access to their personal data and interoperability rights.

bills.title: Conversational AI Disclosure and Safety Requirements

bills.title: Chatbot Nonhuman Disclosures for Minors
bills.summary: Largely identical to Arizona's HB 2311. Would require nonhuman disclosures to minors, restrict engagement optimization, and prohibit minors from accessing sexually explicit content. Unlike the Arizona bill, does not require operators to provide privacy or account-management tools for minor users. Introduced by the Senate Committee on Technology.

bills.title: Chatbot Safety, Privacy, and Age Verification

bills.title: AI Therapy Restrictions and Disclosure Requirements
bills.summary: Largely identical to Illinois' HB 1806. Would prohibit licensed professionals (therapy providers) from using AI for anything beyond defined 'supplementary support' (e.g., preparing client records, analyzing anonymized data, identifying external resources) unless the client is informed in writing and provides consent. Also bans entities from offering or advertising AI-delivered therapy to the public unless conducted by a licensed professional, with exemptions for religious counseling, peer support, and educational resources.

bills.summary: Would set comprehensive requirements for employers' use of automated decision-making and electronic monitoring tools in the workplace.

bills.title: Chatbot Disclosures and Minor Protections
bills.summary: Would require disclosures to minors, implementation of safety protocols, and privacy/account management functions for parents of minor users of chatbot services.

bills.title: Chatbot Safety for Minors
bills.summary: Would prohibit providing unsafe chatbot features to minors including simulating companionship, facilitating self-harm, encouraging secrecy or isolation, and generating sexually explicit conduct.

bills.title: Companion Chatbot Age Verification
bills.summary: Modeled on the federal CHAT Act, requiring age verification for individuals seeking access to a companion chatbot.

bills.title: Companion Chatbot Framework
bills.summary: Would establish a companion chatbot framework similar to California's SB 243, with some additional requirements. Would require clear and conspicuous disclosures to users and mandate safety protocols including referrals to crisis resources when users express self-harm ideation. Includes additional protections for minors, prohibiting chatbots from simulating emotional dependence or making users believe they interact with a human, while requiring recurring three-hour disclosures and banning sexually explicit visual content. Also would prohibit engagement-maximization or reward mechanisms directed at minors. Creates a private right of action.

bills.title: GenAI Content Provenance and Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require large online platforms to detect, disclose, and preserve provenance data and provide user tools to inspect that information. Device manufacturers would be required to embed latent disclosures; GenAI providers (with >1 million monthly users) would be required to include latent disclosures in AI-generated or substantially modified content; and there would be new protections and takedown procedures for non-consensual AI-generated intimate images.

bills.title: AI Companion Chatbot Comprehensive Regulation
bills.summary: Would establish a comprehensive regulatory framework for AI companion chatbots, requiring operators to comply with the Utah Consumer Privacy Act, including prohibiting undisclosed advertising within conversations. For minors, mandates hourly disclosures and referrals to crisis resources when suicidal ideation is detected, and prohibits encouraging illegal substance use, sexual conduct, or other harmful behavior. Also limits collection of minors' data to what is necessary for core functionality and prohibits the sale of users' personal data. The Division of Consumer Protection would be authorized to establish age assurance standards through rulemaking, with compliant operators eligible for a safe harbor.

bills.title: ADMT and Profiling Privacy Law Updates
bills.summary: Would update Utah's data privacy laws by introducing new definitions for automated decision making and profiling.

bills.title: AI Regulatory Sandbox for Public Education
bills.summary: Would establish an Artificial Intelligence Regulatory Sandbox for public education, allowing pilot programs for testing AI tools under defined safety, privacy, and oversight requirements. Approved pilots would require educator supervision, parental notice and opt-out rights, student data protections, safety testing, and evaluation of educational outcomes. Follows SB 149 (2024) which created a broader AI sandbox program in Utah.

bills.title: Health AI Regulation
bills.summary: Health AI bill that passed first chamber.

bills.title: Companion Chatbot Regulation
bills.summary: As amended, would regulate companion chatbots, including disclosure mandates, minor-specific requirements, and creating a safety protocol. Follows the California SB 243 model.
bills.status_detail: Passed the House (Senate Bill passing second chamber)

bills.title: AI Self-Harm Prohibition, CSAM Offenses, and Developer Liability
bills.summary: Would prohibit the development or distribution of AI systems intended to promote self-harm. Also creates new criminal offenses for the development or distribution of AI-generated CSAM. Provides immunity to AI developers from liability for damages arising from misuse of their systems by third parties, except when the developer should have known the system would be used for illegal purposes.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: Alabama enacted SB 161, the first App Store Accountability Act (ASAA) enacted in 2026. Differs from prior ASAA laws by extending age verification and parental consent requirements to existing accounts, requiring parental consent for pre-installed apps, removing application exemptions, and adopting a definition for 'in-app purchases.'
bills.status_detail: Enacted (signed into law) - first ASAA signed in 2026

bills.title: Comprehensive Privacy
bills.summary: A Connecticut-style comprehensive privacy bill passed the House by a vote of 104-0. Alabama came close to enacting a comprehensive privacy law last year but fell short.

bills.title: Comprehensive Privacy with Substantive Data Minimization
bills.summary: Novel comprehensive privacy bill with requirements including: substantive data minimization for collection, use, retention, and sharing of personal information; distinctions between business, commercial, and operational purposes; opt-in consent for precise geolocation data beyond service necessity; restrictions on disclosing or selling personal information of consumers known or recklessly disregarded to be age 16 or younger; and data broker registration requirements.

bills.title: Privacy-Protective Default Settings
bills.summary: CCPA amendment that would require an operating system or application to configure a user's default privacy setting to be the most privacy protective setting offered, and would prohibit changing a user's privacy setting without the user's explicit consent.

bills.title: Mortgage Applicant Data Privacy
bills.summary: Would prohibit a person from selling to a third party personal information of a mortgage applicant that was collected by the person during the mortgage application process.

bills.title: Biometric and Automated Content Recognition Data Protection
bills.summary: KCDPA amendment that would add 'automatic content recognition data' captured by a smart television or smart monitor as a category of sensitive data.

bills.title: Consumer Health Data Protections (MNCDPA Amendment)
bills.summary: Proposed amendments to the MNCDPA that were introduced last year are now active again. An amendment to HF 2700 pares back some proposed changes; under the most recent text, the bill would add Connecticut SB 3-style protections for consumer health data and add protections against 'sharing' sensitive data (requiring opt-in consent). Received committee hearing this week.
bills.status_detail: Active after hiatus; received committee hearing

bills.title: Consumer Health Data Protections (MNCDPA Amendment, Senate Companion)
bills.summary: Senate companion to HF 2700. Proposed amendments to the MNCDPA that were introduced last year are now active again, adding Connecticut SB 3-style protections for consumer health data and protections against 'sharing' sensitive data (requiring opt-in consent). Received committee hearing this week.
bills.status_detail: Active after hiatus; received committee hearing

bills.title: New York Health Information Privacy Act (NYHIPA)
bills.summary: Reintroduction of the New York Health Information Privacy Act (NYHIPA), a broad My Health My Data-style bill that was vetoed by Governor Hochul last year. This iteration includes a changed definition of 'regulated health information,' clarification that consumer rights requests must be verified, expanded permissible processing purposes under the substantive data minimization requirements (capturing product improvement and development), and removal of the 24-hour waiting period for obtaining valid authorization for processing purposes not strictly necessary under the law.
bills.status_detail: Reintroduced after prior year gubernatorial veto

bills.title: IoT Camera Device Privacy
bills.summary: Would regulate manufacturers and operators of internet-connected camera devices (e.g., video doorbells), requiring affirmative opt-in consent, separate from general terms of service, to: enable any 'coordinated surveillance feature'; use footage for purposes other than services directly requested by the owner; retain captured footage not activated with a paid subscription for more than 72 hours; or condition basic functionality on owner participation in a 'coordinated surveillance feature.' Also imposes transparency requirements and limits law enforcement access to footage.

bills.title: ISP Privacy
bills.summary: Would prohibit a broadband internet access service provider from using, disclosing, selling, or permitting access to customer personal information without prior opt-in consent, and prohibit ISPs from refusing service, charging higher prices, or offering discounts based on a customer's consent decision. Includes exceptions for personal information use 'necessary' for providing the broadband internet access service.

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: App Store Accountability Act (ASAA) bill. Passed the Senate committee as amended on February 20 and is now up for consideration in the full Senate, where it has been quickly scheduled for a committee hearing.
bills.status_detail: Passed Senate committee as amended (February 20); scheduled for Senate hearing

bills.title: Direct-to-Consumer Genetic Testing Privacy
bills.summary: A direct-to-consumer genetic testing privacy bill including consumer data rights, consent requirements, and data security obligations. Passed the House on February 25.

bills.title: Geolocation Data Sale Prohibition
bills.summary: A VCDPA amendment that would prohibit a controller from selling precise geolocation data. The House Communications, Technology and Innovation committee reported the bill favorably on February 23. Previously passed the Senate on February 3.
bills.status_detail: Passed House committee (reported February 23); previously passed Senate February 3

bills.title: Reproductive Privacy GLBA Data-Level Exception
bills.summary: Would amend the Virginia Consumer Protection Act to add a GLBA data-level exception to the consent requirement for obtaining, disclosing, selling, or disseminating personally identifiable reproductive or sexual health information. The House General Laws committee favorably reported the bill. Previously passed the Senate on January 27.
bills.status_detail: Passed House committee (favorably reported); previously passed Senate January 27

bills.title: App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: App Store Accountability Act (ASAA) bill passed the Assembly with amendments on February 19 and is pending Senate consideration. Amendments adopted prior to passage include: allowing developers to direct an app store to prevent minors from downloading the developer's apps; providing developer exceptions for adult-only account verification processes and COPPA compliance; removing the private right of action; and creating an exemption for 'video service franchise' as defined under existing law. The Wisconsin Assembly adjourned early for the year, which may pose challenges if the Senate seeks to further amend the bill.
bills.status_detail: Passed Assembly with amendments (February 19); pending Senate consideration
